translations.text: They shall wash its internal organs and its legs with water, and the priest shall offer them all on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a sacrifice with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
If someone brings an offering, it shall be fine flour. He shall pour oil over it and put frankincense on it, for it is a sacrifice.
And the two kidneys and all the fat on them, including what is on the thighs, and the lobe of the liver together with the kidneys—he shall remove them from there.

The priest shall put some of the bull’s blood on the horns of the incense altar before the Lord, which is in the tent of testimony. He shall pour all the bull’s blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering, which is at the entrance to the tent of testimony.
He shall remove all its fat from it and offer it on the altar.
When he is informed of the sin he has committed in this matter, he shall bring his offering: a female sheep from the flock, without blemish, for the sin he has committed.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

They shall keep a fire burning on the altar; it shall not go out. The priest shall burn wood on it in the morning and arrange the burnt offering on it. He shall offer the fat of the peace offering on it.
He shall offer all the [?] upon it, the fat tail and all the fat on the internal organs.
He shall bring a contribution to the Lord from all his offerings and give it to the priest who pours out the blood of the peace offering. It shall belong to that priest.
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: Whoever brings a peace offering to the Lord shall bring his gift to the Lord from the peace offering.
You shall eat it in the holy place, for this is your prescribed share and the prescribed share of your children, to belong to you from the Lord’s burnt offerings. For this is what I was commanded.”
And the ostrich, the owl, the gull and those like them, and the hawk and those like it.

The priest shall examine him on the seventh day for the second time. If the sore is darkened or faded, and the sore has not changed in the skin of his body, the priest shall declare him clean, for what is on him is a spot. He shall wash his clothes and be clean.
The priest shall examine him, and if the sore has turned white, the priest shall declare the sore clean, and he shall be clean.
The priest shall examine him on the seventh day. If it has spread across the skin of his body, the priest shall declare him unclean. It is leprosy that has broken out in his burn.

The priest shall look at the sore. If it appears deeper than the skin of his body and there is thin yellowish hair in it, the priest shall declare him unclean, for it is a scaly sore: leprosy of his head or leprosy of his beard.
If a man or a woman has a white, shining patch on the skin of the body,
but the hair of his head has fallen out at the front, this is frontal baldness—that is, a bald forehead. He is clean.
If a garment has a leprous sore in it, whether a garment of plant fiber, or a garment of linen or wool,
or in the warp or the weft, or in linen or wool, or in a hide or any hide used for making things,
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
the priest shall order them to remove the stones on which the leprous sore has appeared. They shall throw them outside the city into an unclean place.
They shall scrape the inside of the house all around and pour out the earth they have scraped off outside the city into an unclean place.

But if the priest comes and enters and looks, and the leprous sore has not spread in the house after the house was plastered, the priest shall declare the house clean, because that mark has disappeared from it.
On the eighth day she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them before the priest at the entrance to the tent of testimony.
Aaron shall bring his bull as a sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household.

And he shall take some of the bull’s blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the east side of the atonement cover. He shall sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times in front of the atonement cover.

And he shall slaughter the bull for the sins of the people before the Lord, and bring some of its blood inside the curtain. He shall do with its blood as he did with the bull’s blood, and sprinkle its blood on the atonement cover and in front of the atonement cover.
And he shall place the fat of the sin offering on the altar.

So that the Israelites may bring the sacrifices they intend to slaughter in the fields, and bring them before the Lord, to the entrance of the tent of testimony, to the priest, and slaughter them as peace offerings to the Lord.
You shall keep all my commands and all my judgments and carry them out. A person who carries them out will live by them. I am the Lord your God.
You must not uncover the nakedness of your sister, your father’s daughter or your mother’s daughter, whether [?] born at home or born outside.
For the people of the land who lived there before you committed all these detestable acts, and the land became defiled.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
And when you reap the harvest of your land, you must not reap your field completely. You must not gather up what falls to the ground from your harvest.
You must not go about deceitfully among your people. You must not gather deceitfully to threaten your neighbor’s life, for I am the Lord your God.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

Speak to the Israelites, saying: If anyone among the Israelites, or among the foreigners who have joined Israel, gives any of his offspring to a ruler, he must be put to death. The people of the land shall stone him with stones.
And anyone who sleeps with his father’s wife has uncovered his father’s nakedness. They must both be put to death; both of them are guilty.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
No one among the descendants of Aaron the priest who has a physical defect may approach to offer a sacrifice to his God, because he has a defect. He must not approach to present the gifts of his God.

And if a priest’s daughter becomes a widow or is divorced and has no offspring, she shall return to her father’s house as in her youth and eat her father’s bread. But no outsider of foreign birth may eat it.
And anyone who unknowingly eats any of the holy things shall add a fifth of its value to it and give the holy thing to the priest.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
And you must not profane the name of the Holy One. I will be held holy among the Israelites, for I am the Lord who makes you holy.
And the first day shall be proclaimed holy for you. You must not do any ordinary work on it.
And you shall bring your burnt offerings and present them to the Lord for seven days. The seventh day shall be proclaimed holy for you. You must not do any ordinary work on it.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
And you shall offer one male goat from the goats as a sin offering, and two lambs a year old as a peace offering, together with the bread of the first produce.
And you shall proclaim that day holy for you. You must not do any work on it. It is not fitting for it to be a perpetual statute for you in all your settlements throughout your generations.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
And the first day shall be proclaimed holy. You must not do any work that is improper.

And on the first day you shall take fruit from beautiful trees, and [?], or palm branches, and branches of trees with abundant leaves, and a chaste tree—that is, a willow—from a stream or flowing water. You shall rejoice before the Lord your God and celebrate the Lord’s festival for seven days each year.
He shall light the lamp on the holy lampstand before the Lord until morning.
From the Israelites at all times, as an everlasting covenant.
There shall be one law for the foreign resident and the native, for I am the Lord your God.
And the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying:
But if you say, “What will you eat in this seventh year, when we do not sow and you do not gather your crops?”
But if your brother who lives with you becomes poor and sells part of his inheritance, and his nearest relative wishes to redeem his brother’s inheritance, he shall redeem it.
But if he has no close relative, and he acquires the means and finds the man [?] for his redemption,
You must not take interest from him or charge him extra. You shall fear your God, for I am the Lord, so that your brother may live with you.
You must not make handmade idols for yourselves, or [?], or set up a pillar for yourselves, or place a stone for worship in your land to bow down to it. I am the Lord your God.
You shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall before you in fear.
Ten of you shall pursue a hundred men, and a hundred of you shall pursue ten thousand men. Your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.
And I will scatter you among the nations, and the sword shall come against you and destroy you, and your cities shall lie deserted.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
